title: ShipClass
description: The design. Stats are authored here; named hulls reference a class and add only identity, status and refit deltas. Two authoring styles are legal and may coexist in one file: the LITERAL style (propulsion/armament as flat figures) for historical seed data, and the COMPONENT style (machinery.fits, batteries[].component, provisions[]) for any fleet built on an equipment catalog. A class using the component style is the one the provision-match cost rule (conventions 6) can actually price.

treaty_category.description: What the treaty engine audits, independent of the sim type.

generation.description: standardized: a hull drawn once and built unchanged for decades, where the class IS the program.

parent_class.description: For an improved build of the same hull (Japan: -kai). The delta belongs in `changes`.

changes.description: One line: what this class changes from parent_class.

cost_gold.description: First-of-line price before learning-curve discounts. 1 gold = 1 kg fine gold.

durability.description: Structural damage capacity, orthogonal to the armor model.

empty_tons.description: As completed: hull, machinery, armament, fixed equipment. No crew, ammunition, stores or liquids.

standard_tons.description: The Washington standard: complete, manned, ready for sea with ammunition and war stores, WITHOUT fuel or reserve feed water.

full_load_tons.description: Standard plus every liquid the hull carries. full_load minus standard IS the fuel block and nothing else.

propulsion.description: LITERAL style. Use for a navy with no engine-cartridge SKUs, which states its cruising speed directly here (conventions 5). Mutually exclusive in practice with `machinery`.

battery.description: COMPONENT style, submarines. The storage battery is a component with generations, and this row is the exact analogue of the machinery row: the cell the class is launched with, how many of them, and the generations she can be RE-CELLED to. Groups replace through a deck hatch one at a time without cutting the pressure hull, which is why a boat's battery can be renewed at a fitting-out berth and why an old hull is worth re-celling at all. ⚠ A `bat` code belongs HERE AND NOWHERE ELSE: never in `sensors` (a cell is not a sensor), never as a `batteries[]` component (that array is weapons, and the collision of names is unfortunate), and never in `possible_upgrades` — a re-cell is this row's own refit, exactly as an engine change is the machinery row's.

component.description: The cell fitted as launched. Must be of family `bat`.

kwh_total.description: Derived: cells x the cell's own kWh. Stated because the interesting figure is per ton of submerged displacement, and that division is what separates a good cell from a boat designed around one.

refit_groups.description: Later cell generations this hull can be re-celled to. Exempt from as-launched discipline by the same rule that exempts machinery refit groups (conventions 7).

machinery.description: COMPONENT style. A hull of identical bays, each taking an engine cartridge. Fleet speed and range are growth curves, not fixed numbers: one entry per available cartridge generation, each with its own shp/speed/range.

cruise_bank.description: Bays lit on passage. A per-class datum, NOT derived from the bay count. On a diesel-electric hull the cruise is set by the motors' demand and the lit bank throttles to it.

swap.description: How a cartridge is exchanged and how long it takes — the whole point of the bay.

motor_shp.description: Electric drive: the motors' output, where it differs from generating power.

speed_kn.description: At service displacement: standard plus two-thirds of the PROPULSION bunkers. Aviation fuel never enters the speed basis.

condition.description: Where a hull quotes speeds at a stated load, e.g. 'at merchant full load'.

speed_submerged.description: Submarines. A boat that fights submerged states its submerged speeds as first-class data, not as a footnote to a surface figure.

avgas_tons.description: Aviation stores. Enters full load, never the speed basis.

armament.description: LITERAL style, for historical seed data.

batteries.description: COMPONENT style. Each entry names the SKU it fights, so a turret change is a data change and a dual-purpose battery is one entry rather than two.

spec.description: LITERAL alternative to `component`, for a fitting that lies outside the navy's own Mark/Type sequence and therefore has no SKU. Exactly one of `component` or `spec` must be present. A main battery ALWAYS lives here, never in the class's `armament` block, so that anything reading `batteries[]` finds it.

pattern.description: The navy's own pattern year for a fitting with no Mark/Type number.

items.description: COMPONENT style. Each entry names the SKU it fights, so a turret change is a data change and a dual-purpose battery is one entry rather than two. EXACTLY ONE of `component` (a SKU) or `spec` (a literal, for a fitting outside the navy's Mark/Type sequence) must be present. Every BB/BC/CA/CL/DD carries exactly one entry with role 'main'; tools/validate.py enforces it.

box_mm.description: Machinery/magazine box, for a hull armored to a box rather than a belt.

features.description: Survivability architecture that is not a thickness: avgas cofferdams, CO2 inerting, split switchboards and casualty power, subdivision. On some hulls this IS the protection scheme.

flight_deck_mm.description: Armored flight deck. Distinct from `deck_mm`, which on a carrier is the hangar deck.

aircraft_capacity.description: Catapult ships only. A carrier states hangar/deck_park and lets capacity be DERIVED.

catapult.description: The catapult-and-crane SKU the hull carries. A rating alone is not a reference: the line is in the equipment catalog and the hull points at it.

deck_park_m2.description: Handling and ranging area. Stows knocked-down spares; adds NO embarked capacity.

hangar_upper_cycle_deck_m2.description: Upper hangar deck, where airplanes are struck down, respotted, armed and fueled between launches. Sums with the lower deck to hangar_m2.

hangar_lower_workshop_deck_m2.description: Lower hangar deck, where maintenance is done and knocked-down spares are stowed. Sums with the upper deck to hangar_m2.

provisions.description: The hull's declared interfaces (conventions 6) — including the ones with nothing in them. An empty wired gallery, a plated-over barbette ring, a sponson foundation for a landing area nobody can yet describe: these are the provision habit, and they are DATA, not prose. Cost follows provision match: provisioned = trivial cost and days; non-provisioned = structural-work pricing.

interface.description: Must match the `interface` of the component line that fills it.

fitted.description: How many are filled as launched. fitted < count is the empty provision; it is not an error.

for.description: Component code or kit the provision is cut for, where the hull knows. Often a set that does not exist yet.

kits.description: Conversion kits this hull carries the fittings for. Kits are fittings, never upgrades.

fitouts.description: A merchant hull's alternative completions. One hull, one displacement; a fitout redistributes weight, it does not create a second ship.

type_year.description: Japan: the year in the class's own designation. A nation whose designation system is not year-based — Britain's mark_roman, Germany's konstruktionsjahr — HAS NO TYPE YEAR AND OMITS THIS FIELD, because a Mark number is a serial and not a date. Where present it is the as-launched discipline's reference year unless as_launched_year overrides it.

as_launched_year.description: The year the as-launched sheet describes: the first ship of the class to commission carrying the outfit set out here, or, for a class that never commissions, the design year. OVERRIDES type_year as the as-launched discipline's reference year, and exists because the two coincide only in Japan. A British class is named for the year it was ORDERED and commissions three to five years later — the Incomparables are the 1931 program and their sheet is 1934 — so without this field the discipline is enforced against the wrong date in both directions.

hulls_aggregate.description: For flotilla classes tracked in bulk instead of (or alongside) named hulls.

possible_upgrades.description: Later generations of every family this class's own rows name. Engine codes never appear here (machinery.fits carries them); kit codes never appear here.
